newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end lower on A share slump.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end lower on A share slump.

text.p: The Shenzhen B share index closed lower on Tuesday in response to steep falls on the A share market triggered by renewed warnings from the securities authorities on the risks of stock investment, brokers said.
Caution is likely to dominate the markets in the next few sessions due to the repeated calls in official newspapers for risk-control awareness, they said.
The B index lost 1.08 points or 0.67 percent to 159.33 on turnover of HK$64.57 million from Monday's HK$68.4 million.
The A index fell 12.61 points or 2.69 percent to 456.38 on turnover of 11.7 billion yuan from Monday's 13.3 billion yuan.

"The B shares were pushed down by falls amongst their A share counterparts but the downward potential on the B share market is limited as it has only registered marginal rises since the beginning of this year," an analyst said.
"Whether the A share market continues to fall sharply depends on whether the securities authorities announce any specific measures," the analyst said.
On the B share market, Chiwan Wharf was the worst performer, falling HK$0.37 or 6.49 percent to HK$5.33 on volume of 138,700 shares.
The company, which handles port facilities in Shenzhen, posted a 14 percent drop in its 1996 net profit on Tuesday.
Chiwan proposed a cash dividend of 0.169 yuan per share based on 1996 profits, the company said in its annual report.
"Investors were disappointed by the company's dividend plan," a second analyst said.
